brief: BofA's out-of-consensus call is for the Fed to hike two more times in 2026, 25bp each in October and December, following the September 25bp hike, for a modest 75bp cycle. The reasoning centers on the nominal economy: nominal spending is up 6.3% y/y, above the 5% threshold that historically precedes core PCE overshooting 2%, so robust nominal growth both raises inflation-persistence risk and lowers the recession risk from hiking. Two factors beyond the Fed's control sealed the September hike: oil prices rising into the meeting and a backfired Treasury buyback program that spiked yields and raised de-anchoring concerns. Aug retail sales beat expectations, lifting BofA's 3Q PCE tracking to 3.4% q/q saar and 3Q GDP tracking to 3.0%. BofA expects core PCE to ease toward 2.5% by the middle of next year as tariff and Iran effects roll off, flattering Chair Warsh's legacy. Risk: if wages reaccelerate as the u-rate falls, or Iran-driven supply inflation proves stickier than assumed, 75bp may not suffice, forcing a choice between prolonged above-target inflation or a harder landing.
